content: The Sloane Hospital for Women serves as the obstetrics and gynecology division of New York-Presbyterian Hospital and is part of the Department of Obstetrics and Gynecology at Columbia University College of Physicians and Surgeons in New York City. It was originally established as the Sloane Maternity Hospital in 1886, thanks to a donation from William D. Sloane and his wife, Emily Thorn Vanderbilt Sloane, who was the granddaughter of Cornelius Vanderbilt. The hospital was the first in New York City dedicated exclusively to women's healthcare. The facility was initially located on the campus of Columbia P&S in Midtown Manhattan, at Amsterdam Avenue and 59th Street. It opened in early 1888 and quickly gained recognition for its exceptional sanitary standards and low mortality rates. Notably, it was the first hospital in the United States to integrate obstetrics and gynecology into a single discipline. In 1910, the hospital was renamed the Sloane Hospital for Women. A year later, in 1911, a new surgical building was added, funded by the Sloane family. In 1925, the hospital became part of Presbyterian Hospital, which was affiliated with Columbia P&S. By 1928, the Sloane Hospital for Women relocated to its current location on 168th Street in the Washington Heights neighborhood of northern Manhattan. At this new site, it retained its name and occupied several floors within the Presbyterian Hospital building. Over the years, the Sloane Hospital for Women has played a pivotal role in advancing the field of obstetrics and gynecology. It has been at the forefront of numerous medical innovations, including the development of the Apgar score, the introduction of Rh immunoglobulin (Rhogam) to prevent Rh incompatibility, and the refinement of amniocentesis as a diagnostic tool.
